extracted.intended_audience: scientists, peer reviewers, and rationalist-community members interested in improving scientific methods and publication norms
extracted.subtask_description: An essay proposing high-level reforms to scientific practice and reviewer norms (preregistration, reducing experimenter bias, and statistical reform). Useful as guidance for reviewers, editors, and researchers about what to demand of empirical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication bias / preregistration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals should only accept experiments registered in a public database before they began.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment: reviewers and editors should require pre-registration as an acceptance condition to combat publication bias. Anti-pattern: accepting post-hoc analyses or selectively reported positive results without a prior registry entry. Scoring note: treat studies with pre-registration as confirmatory evidence; downgrade unregistered studies for potential selection/reporting bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish exploratory vs confirmatory results
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should treat unregistered exploratory results differently from confirmatory tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: explicitly label analyses as exploratory if not pre-registered; do not let exploratory findings be presented as pre-planned confirmations. Anti-pattern: ratifying unregistered, post-hoc hypotheses as if they were pre-specified. Reviewer role: demand clarity about which results were pre-specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimenter bias mitigation / rationality training
rubrics_metrics.description: Train scientists in rationality skills to reduce cognitive errors (experimenter bias).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for reviewers/editors: evaluate whether authors took steps to mitigate cognitive biases (blinding, pre-specification, independent analysis, training). Encourage institutional or curricular rationality/statistics education. Anti-pattern: relying solely on formal procedures without attention to researchers' reasoning habits; scoring: papers showing explicit bias-mitigation practices score higher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of methodological safeguards (control groups, blinding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use control groups, blind and double-blind studies where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should check for appropriate experimental design features (controls, blinding) and penalize studies lacking them when they are feasible. Example: lack of blinding in subjective outcome studies is a major weakness. Scoring: presence and correct implementation of controls/blinding improves methodological score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods: favor Bayesian inference / improve statistical education
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace frequentist methods with Bayesian inference; improve statistical education to address 'bad statistics'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess whether statistical methods are appropriate and whether authors understand their inferential framework. Anti-patterns: blind reliance on p-values, misinterpretation of statistical significance, underpowered studies. Guidance: prefer coherent Bayesian analyses where feasible and demand proper interpretation of uncertainty; encourage better statistical training for researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer enforcement role (do not ratify pre-registration breaches)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reviewer's job is not to ratify pre-registration breaches and is to demand pre-registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should refuse to treat post-hoc or unregistered analyses as confirmatory and should require authors to correct the record or reclassify analyses. Editorial policy implication: peer reviewers act as gatekeepers enforcing pre-registration norms rather than excusing deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and public registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Require public disclosure of experiment registration and methodology before experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages full transparency: public registry entries, methods and analysis plans available for scrutiny. Anti-pattern: opaque methods or undisclosed analytic choices. Reviewer action: verify existence and content of registry entries; request supplementary materials or raw data when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism as a limiting reagent
rubrics_metrics.description: Rationality training and skepticism are the limiting reagents, not formality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for reviewers: apply active skepticism and rational critique beyond checking formal boxes. Anti-pattern: procedural compliance without substantive critical evaluation. Scoring implication: work demonstrating robust skeptical appraisal and self-critique is stronger.
